title: Only the validator who raised an issue may declare it resolved, giving each validator an individual veto over the Spell
content:
Two provisions combine into a strong individual power. A.1.10.2.4.12.4.4: "**Only the validator who raised the issue is permitted to consider an issue as resolved**, and any unresolved issue will prevent the Spell from passing validation." A.1.10.2.4.12.4.2: a Spell fails validation when "one or more issues are identified" or "reported issues remain unresolved to the satisfaction of the Spell validator."

So validation outcome is not a majority verdict or a facilitator's judgment call. One validator with an unsatisfied concern is sufficient to withhold a pass, and no amount of agreement from others can close their issue for them.

This is the necessary complement to the assume-malice rule. Requiring adversarial scepticism would be empty if the party being doubted, or a consensus of colleagues, could simply mark the concern addressed. Ownership of resolution is what converts scepticism into leverage.

What keeps it from being an obstruction tool is that validation failure is not the same as a veto over the vote. The Spell is already live on the Voting Portal; failing validation is a *signal to SKY holders and delegates*, not a technical block. The validator's power is to publish a well-founded refusal, and the ecosystem decides what to do with it — which is why A.1.10.2.4.12.4.1 prefers validation to be public.

The design intentionally accepts noise in exchange for capture-resistance. A process that requires consensus to raise an alarm can be silenced by capturing the consensus; one where any single participant can withhold approval cannot.
description: A.1.10.2.4.12.4.2 fails a Spell on any single unresolved issue, and A.1.10.2.4.12.4.4 bars anyone else — including the Core Facilitator — from closing it on the raiser's behalf.
